key: AGNI inflamed hath sent to heaven his lustre: he shines forth widely turning unto Morning. Eastward the ladle goes that brings all blessing, praising the Godswith homage and oblation.
s: Opening a short hymn of kindling and offering, the verse turns from Agni’s flame to the ladle; Sāyaṇa, on 5.28.1, reads the one going eastward with ladle and oblation as Viśvavārā, a woman of Atri’s line whom he takes as the hymn’s seer.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.28.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 199496 (2019)

opened.locator: commentary on 5.28.1, and the hymn introduction naming the seer

evidence.words: “नमोभिः स्तोत्रैः "देवान् इन्द्रादीन् “ईळाना स्तुवती “हविषा पुरोडाशादिलक्षणेन युक्त्या “घृताची घृताच्या स्रुचा सहिता "विश्ववारा सर्वमपि पापरूपं शत्रुं वारयित्र्येतन्नामिका “प्राची प्राङ्मुखी सती “एति । एवंभूतमग्निं प्रतिगच्छति ॥
evidence.gloss: Praising the gods, Indra and the rest, with hymns, joined with the oblation of cakes and the like, holding the ladle of ghee, she who is named Viśvavārā, the warder-off of every enemy that is sin, goes facing east: she goes toward Agni, who is as described.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 5.28.1, at [381,1]; the app’s own spacing slip ‘Godswith’ is kept as printed). Sāyaṇa on 5.28.1 takes the feminine subject who goes facing east (prācī), praising the gods, with the oblation and the ghee ladle (ghṛtācī, glossed ghṛtācyā srucā sahitā) as the woman named Viśvavārā, not as the ladle; his hymn introduction says the seer of this hymn is Viśvavārā, born in Atri’s line (अत्रिगोत्रोत्पन्ना विश्ववारानामिका अस्य सूक्तस्य ऋषिः), and Wilson note 2 reports both. Plain sense faithful: a six-verse Agni hymn of kindling and offering, the verse moving from the flame to the offering. Revision 199496 dated 2019-04-14 by the Wikisource API.
